_comment: Bootstrap hypothesis, not gospel. This file decides which cards get spent
credits first; the scanner replaces the guesswork with data as coverage
grows. Set ids follow pokemontcg.io. `run.py catalog --verify-sets` reports
any id that returns zero cards so typos surface immediately.
Prior: PSA 9 profitability lives almost entirely in vintage. Modern PSA 9s
typically fetch 30-50% of the PSA 10 and lose money after fees, so modern
sets are seeded at low priority and included mainly as a control group.

sets.name: Base Set
sets.why: off-centre cuts + deep demand; the canonical vintage grade

sets.name: Team Rocket
sets.why: dark holos show edge wear badly

sets.name: Neo Genesis
sets.why: factory print lines cap many copies at 8

sets.name: Neo Destiny
sets.why: print lines; Shining subset is the scarce tier

sets.name: Aquapolis
sets.why: Crystal subset: layered foil, very few clean copies

sets.name: Skyridge
sets.why: smallest WOTC print run; Crystals are the hardest tier to grade

sets.name: Team Rocket Returns
sets.why: start of the Gold Star run

sets.name: Dragon Frontiers
sets.why: Gold Stars incl. the most chased copies

sets.name: Evolving Skies
sets.why: modern control group; alt arts are condition sensitive

cards.name: Charizard
cards.why: Crystal Charizard: benchmark for a scarce, hard-to-grade vintage holo

cards.name: Ho-Oh
cards.why: Crystal Ho-Oh: layered foil, very thin PSA 10 population

cards.name: Kingdra
cards.why: Crystal Kingdra, frequently cited Aquapolis chase

cards.name: Charizard
cards.why: deepest demand in vintage; useful as a liquidity benchmark

cards.name: Umbreon Star
cards.why: Gold Star cited as profitable even at PSA 9
